```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("SanzCodina_2024_cefiderocol"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("SanzCodina_2024_cefiderocol"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkae359> (open access, PMC11638555)

Sanz-Codina and colleagues gave eight healthy men a single 2 g intravenous
dose of cefiderocol over 3 h and measured total plasma concentrations,
unbound plasma concentrations (ultrafiltration at 3, 4 and 7 h) and unbound
interstitial concentrations in subcutaneous adipose and skeletal muscle tissue
by microdialysis. The final population model is a two-compartment model fitted
to UNBOUND concentrations with a constant estimated fraction unbound (`fu`);
the two tissue concentrations are the peripheral-compartment concentration
multiplied by a tissue scaling factor (`TFsub`, `TFmus`).

# Population

Eight healthy male volunteers aged 18-55 years (mean 34.9 +/- 8.9 years) with
body mass index 19-30 kg/m^2 (mean 24.6 +/- 1.1 kg/m^2) and a Cockcroft-Gault
creatinine clearance above 90 mL/min, studied at the Medical University of
Vienna (Methods, "Study population and in vivo procedures"; Results, "Study
population and safety"). Race was not reported. The model has no covariates:
the authors state that the small, homogeneous cohort precluded a covariate
analysis.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("SanzCodina_2024_cefiderocol")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, unbound-referenced) | log(11.0) L/h | Table 2, 'CL (L/h)' |
| `lvc` (Vc, unbound-referenced) | log(11.3) L | Table 2, 'Vc (L)' |
| `lq` (Q12) | log(25.3) L/h | Table 2, 'Q12 (L/h)' |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(15.1) L | Table 2, 'Vp (L)' |
| `lfu` (fraction unbound) | log(0.639) | Table 2, 'fu' |
| `lkp_adipose` (TFsub) | log(0.943) | Table 2, 'TFsub' |
| `lkp_muscle` (TFmus) | log(0.901) | Table 2, 'TFmus' |
| `etalcl` | 0.0298 (17.4% CV) | Table 2, IIV 'CL (CV%)'; omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1) per Table 2 footnote |
| `etalvc` | 0.0679 (26.5% CV) | Table 2, IIV 'Vc (CV%)' |
| `etalkp_adipose` | 0.0755 (28.0% CV) | Table 2, IIV 'TFsub (CV%)' |
| `etalkp_muscle` | 0.0616 (25.2% CV) | Table 2, IIV 'TFmus (CV%)' |
| `propSd`, `propSd_Cunbound` | 0.0585 | Table 2, 'Propplasma (CV%)' = 5.85 (one plasma error) |
| `propSd_Cadipose`, `propSd_Cmuscle` | 0.303 | Table 2, 'Proptissue (CV%)' = 30.3 (one tissue error) |
| `addSd_Cadipose`, `addSd_Cmuscle` | 2.3 mg/L | Table 2, 'Addtissue (mg/L)' = 2.3 |
| Two-compartment structure, first-order elimination | n/a | Methods 'Population PK analysis'; Results 'Population PK model and PTA analysis' |
| `Cunbound = central / vc`; `Cc = Cunbound / fu` | n/a | Table 2 footnote ('Estimates are based on unbound cefiderocol concentrations'); Methods (fu estimated from total vs unbound) |
| `Cadipose`, `Cmuscle` = TF x `peripheral1 / vp` | n/a | Results: tissue concentrations scaled to the peripheral compartment |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. A virtual cohort of 200 subjects (the trial
had 8) receives the trial regimen, 2 g over 3 h. Random effects are drawn in
base R from the model's omega matrix and passed to a typical-value solve
through `params`, so the cohort depends only on `set.seed()` and is identical
on every machine.

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("SanzCodina_2024_cefiderocol")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)

set.seed(20241211)
n_sub <- 200L
omega <- ui$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_sub * nrow(omega)), n_sub) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)
params <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub), eta)

# All four endpoints are algebraic observables, so observation rows are keyed
# by dvid with an empty cmt; doses go to the central ODE state.
make_events <- function(ids, dose_times, obs_times, dose = 2000, dur = 3) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      amt = dose,
      rate = dose / dur,
      evid = 1L,
      cmt = "central",
      dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events_sd <- make_events(params$id, dose_times = 0, obs_times = seq(0, 8, by = 0.1))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events_sd[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events_sd,
  params = params,
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)

stopifnot(nrow(sim_sd) == n_sub * length(seq(0, 8, by = 0.1)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_sd[, c("Cc", "Cunbound", "Cadipose", "Cmuscle")]))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: visual predictive check

Residual error is added in base R with the Table 2 magnitudes (proportional
for both plasma outputs, combined proportional + additive for the tissues) so
the bands are comparable to the VPC. The dashed lines are the 10th and 90th
percentiles and the solid line the median, as in the paper.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.4}
th <- ui$theta
long_sd <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, Cunbound, Cadipose, Cmuscle) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "output", values_to = "ipred")

set.seed(7)
eps1 <- rnorm(nrow(long_sd))
long_sd <- long_sd |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    prop = dplyr::case_when(
      output == "Cc" ~ th[["propSd"]],
      output == "Cunbound" ~ th[["propSd_Cunbound"]],
      output == "Cadipose" ~ th[["propSd_Cadipose"]],
      output == "Cmuscle" ~ th[["propSd_Cmuscle"]]
    ),
    add = dplyr::case_when(
      output == "Cadipose" ~ th[["addSd_Cadipose"]],
      output == "Cmuscle" ~ th[["addSd_Cmuscle"]],
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    # nlmixr2 combined2: variance = add^2 + (prop * ipred)^2
    dv = ipred + sqrt(add^2 + (prop * ipred)^2) * eps1
  )

panel_labels <- c(
  Cc = "Plasma (total)",
  Cunbound = "Plasma (free)",
  Cadipose = "Subcutis (free)",
  Cmuscle = "Muscle (free)"
)

long_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 1) |>
  dplyr::group_by(output, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(dv, 0.10),
    p50 = quantile(dv, 0.50),
    p90 = quantile(dv, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(panel_labels[output], levels = panel_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = p10), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p90), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~output, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Cefiderocol (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Sanz-Codina 2024 (simulated 10th/50th/90th percentiles)."
  )
```

The shapes match Figure 2: total plasma peaks at the end of the 3 h infusion
(typical-value prediction about 67 mg/L), unbound plasma is about 64% of
total, and the two tissue curves rise more slowly and peak just after the end
of infusion at roughly 35 mg/L (typical value). The 10th-90th percentile band
is wide in tissue because of the large tissue residual error.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the individual predictions (no residual error) of each
unbound output over 0-8 h, matching the non-compartmental analysis of Table 1.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- long_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(output %in% c("Cunbound", "Cadipose", "Cmuscle"), !is.na(ipred)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id,
    time,
    Cc = ipred,
    output = unname(panel_labels[output])
  )

# The solve includes a time-zero observation for every subject; assert it so a
# change to the grid cannot silently drop the AUC anchor.
stopifnot(all(dplyr::summarise(nca_in, t0 = any(time == 0), .by = c(id, output))$t0))

dose_in <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = params$id, output = unique(nca_in$output)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 2000)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | output + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_in, amt ~ time | output + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = 8,
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 1 reports arithmetic means, so the simulated per-subject values are
summarised by their mean before the comparison.

```{r nca-compare}
sim_mean <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(output, PPTESTCD))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~output,           ~half.life, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "Subcutis (free)", 1.82,       41.6,  163.2,
  "Muscle (free)",   1.30,       40.9,  151.7,
  "Plasma (free)",   2.04,       39.9,  162.0
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_mean,
  reference = published,
  by = "output",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "h*mg/L, 0-8 h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. Table 1 NCA (means). * differs by >20%.")

auc_mean <- sim_mean |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(published, output, ref = auclast),
    by = "output"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(auc_mean) == 3L)
# Unbound AUC0-8 is the quantity the model was built to reproduce; a wrong CL,
# volume, fu or scaling factor moves it by tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_mean$pct) < 15))
```

The unbound AUC0-8 in plasma and both tissues is within 4% of Table 1, and
Cmax within 12%. The simulated tissue Cmax is about 10% below the observed
mean; an observed Cmax is the largest of several noisy microdialysate values
(tissue residual error about 30%), which biases it upward relative to the
maximum of a smooth individual prediction. The one starred row is the muscle
half-life: Table 1 gives 1.30 h from the observed microdialysis curves, whereas in
the model every tissue concentration is a constant multiple of the peripheral
compartment and therefore shares the plasma terminal half-life (about 2 h).
The paper notes that the model did not fully capture the shape of the muscle
profile (a possible delay in distribution to muscle).

## Total plasma clearance

The disposition parameters are referenced to unbound drug, so total plasma
clearance is `CL * fu`. The Discussion reports an NCA total clearance of
7.2 L/h.

```{r total-cl}
cl_total <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) * exp(th[["lfu"]])
cl_total
stopifnot(abs(cl_total / 7.2 - 1) < 0.05)
```

# Probability of target attainment (Figure 3)

The paper simulated the first 24 h of 2 g every 8 h, each dose infused over
3 h, and computed the percentage of 0-24 h with the unbound concentration
above the MIC in plasma, subcutis and muscle. The same 200-subject cohort is
used here, on individual predictions.

```{r pta, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
events_md <- make_events(
  params$id,
  dose_times = c(0, 8, 16),
  obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)
)
sim_md <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events_md,
  params = params,
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_md[, c("Cunbound", "Cadipose", "Cmuscle")]))

mics <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
ft_above <- sim_md |>
  dplyr::filter(time < 24) |>
  dplyr::select(id, Cunbound, Cadipose, Cmuscle) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(mic = mics) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ft = 100 * mean(conc > mic), .by = c(id, output, mic))

pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(target = c(75, 95), ft_above) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ft >= target), .by = c(target, output, mic)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(panel_labels[output], levels = panel_labels[-1]))

ggplot(pta, aes(factor(mic), pta, colour = output, group = output)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~target, labeller = labeller(target = function(x) paste0("fT>MIC ", x, "%"))) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)",
    y = "Probability of target attainment (%)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Sanz-Codina 2024."
  )

pta_cell <- function(tgt, out, m) {
  v <- pta$pta[pta$target == tgt & pta$output == out & pta$mic == m]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique PTA row for ", tgt, "/", out, "/", m)
  v
}

pta |>
  dplyr::filter(mic %in% c(4, 8, 16)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("fT>MIC target (%)" = target, "Matrix" = output) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Simulated PTA (%) at MIC 4, 8 and 16 mg/L.")

# The paper's headline: PTA >= 90% up to MIC 4 mg/L in plasma and both tissues
# for the 75% target. The model-true values are ~99%, more than 10 binomial
# standard errors (n = 200) above the 90% line.
for (out in levels(pta$output)) stopifnot(pta_cell(75, out, 4) >= 90)
# Figure 3 shows PTA collapsing between 8 and 32 mg/L (fT>MIC 75%: ~11-18% at
# 16 mg/L; fT>MIC 95%: ~32-40% at 8 mg/L). Bounds sit several binomial
# standard errors wide of those values while still failing for a CL or
# volume off by 25%.
for (out in levels(pta$output)) {
  stopifnot(pta_cell(75, out, 16) < 45, pta_cell(75, out, 32) < 5)
  stopifnot(pta_cell(95, out, 8) > 10, pta_cell(95, out, 8) < 70)
}
```

The simulated curves reproduce Figure 3. For fT>MIC 75%, attainment is
complete up to 4 mg/L and falls to about 80-85% at 8 mg/L and 10-17% at
16 mg/L (Figure 3: about 81-88% and 11-18%). For fT>MIC 95%, attainment at
4 mg/L is 86-88% against about 90-92% in Figure 3, and 30-44% at 8 mg/L
(Figure 3: about 32-40%). Attainment is near zero at 32 mg/L in all three
matrices. The shortfall of about 4 percentage points at 4 mg/L for the 95%
target is under two binomial standard errors of a 200-subject cohort (about
2.4 points), and was not tuned.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Microdialysis observation model.** The paper fitted each recovery-corrected
  microdialysate concentration as the integral of the tissue curve over its
  collection interval. The packaged `Cadipose` and `Cmuscle` are instantaneous
  unbound interstitial concentrations; to fit or compare against raw
  microdialysate data, average them over the collection interval.
- **Shared residual errors.** The paper estimated one proportional error for
  plasma (total and unbound observations) and one combined error for both
  tissues. nlmixr2 carries one error parameter per endpoint, so the shared
  estimates are repeated (`propSd` = `propSd_Cunbound`; the `_Cadipose` and
  `_Cmuscle` pairs are equal). Re-estimating the model would treat them as
  separate parameters.
- **Combined error form.** The paper does not say whether the tissue combined
  error adds standard deviations or variances; the nlmixr2 default
  (`combined2`, variances add) is used.
- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as CV% computed from
  sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1), so the variances are log(CV^2 + 1).
- **PTA.** The PTA simulation uses individual predictions without residual
  error and a 200-subject cohort (the paper used 5000 subjects); whether the
  paper's PTA included residual error is not stated.
- **Naming.** The tissue scaling factors TFsub and TFmus are encoded as the
  partition-coefficient canonicals `lkp_adipose` and `lkp_muscle`; note that
  they scale the peripheral-compartment concentration, not the central plasma
  concentration. The subcutaneous microdialysis probe sampled subcutaneous
  adipose tissue, hence `adipose`.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-10-31).
